title: How Adam Robinson built a brand-led content engine for a bootstrapped SaaS (Retention.com)
summary: Adam Robinson explains why brand and community are the real moats in SaaS without network effects. He covers how he built a LinkedIn audience by working in public, and why he pairs a big free offer with a paid upsell. He also gives his view on churn, premium media content and creator-led distribution.

principles.text: Without network effects, brand and community are a SaaS company's only moats, so invest in them early and for the long haul.
principles.quote: brand and Community are the only Moes you have if you don't have Network effects

principles.text: Working in public only grabs attention when your numbers are impressive. Proof of success earns the audience.
principles.quote: somebody shows up and they're like I have 12 million I with six people and I'm gonna tell you everything I'm doing it's like wow

principles.text: Start on the less crowded social network. LinkedIn had far fewer creators than Twitter, so it gave more reach per effort.
principles.quote: only one to two% of people create content versus Twitter is like almost 5050

principles.text: Keep testing posts until you know what great looks like. After that you can run the content machine indefinitely.
principles.quote: if I'm right about this and I know what great is like I can keep this machine going forever

principles.text: Pair a big free product with a paid time-saving upsell. Free users who already got value will pay to skip the work.
principles.quote: I'm trying to sell this idea that if you want to save time with Integrations pay 500 bucks if you don't knock yourself out with a free app forever

principles.text: A premium content series builds a deep bond with viewers that no ad can match, even if it costs real money.
principles.quote: that person is connected to everything that I am doing in a way that they could not have been any other way
